title: 'High degree of certainty' is undefined in V5, and V5's 'depends mainly on the US government' ignores coupon reinvestment
problem: The case requires teams to define high funding certainty, explain how they evaluated it, and list the assumptions. V5 gives no definition and says each payment 'depends mainly on the US government'. That holds for principal but not coupons: on the WInS-listed holdings about $45k of the $500k depends on reinvesting income at about 5% (kit: $447k at 0%; L03: $455k). The kit's headline 'never short' tests (history since 2000, 149 start years, 13 episodes) use STRIPS, now banned. The WInS-basis tests exist (D_certainty test 3; the 16 Oct number sheet section 3), but V5 does not reflect them, and the team's own trade notes say 'reinvested coupons fund the rest'. Do not quote the replay's '65% of start months' without its size: shortfalls are mostly small (median delivered above $500k; worst about $42k). The 15 Oct brief's 'no payment is missed unless yields fall about 420bp' is a STRIPS-basis line and is wrong for the WInS book.

title: Floor-size rule and the 2027-to-2028 sequence can make the branch vanish
problem: The floor is either 'the remainder' (V5:24) or 'about $150k' (COMPETITION.md:155-156). Under the $150k reading, a 2027 top-up plus a low 2028 yield can squeeze the stock fund to near zero and the 2031 range to almost a point. title: Wrong-way risk: the coupon shortfall and a small 'half Laura keeps' tend to arrive together, but both models assume they are independent
problem: The payments fall short when yields fall and stay low; the backstop is the half of the stock fund Laura keeps. Falling yields often come with recessions and stock falls, so the backstop is smallest when it is needed. The kit's own 2008 replay shows it: Laura keeps $18,446 and the gap beyond her half is $12,047. The 16 Oct sheet's 93-in-100 cover and L03's p5 figures both assume rates and stocks move independently, so they likely overstate cover. (The sign of the stock-bond link changes over time: the sheet notes +0.5 correlation in the last year, when yields rose; UNVERIFIED as a forecast either way.)
